title: TF primitive interface handbook
content:
Purpose
This is a lightweight handbook describing the interface norms and upgrade signals we expect from Terraform primitives used in private deployments (VPC, IAM, and cluster primitives for EKS/GKE/AKS). It is intentionally pragmatic: minimal surface area, strong output contracts, and clear upgrade/migration paths. Use this as the source-of-truth for module reviewers and for automated compatibility checks.

Goals and principles
- Minimal public surface: expose only what consumers actually need. Keep inputs opt-in, sensible defaults for region/account, and explicit booleans for opt-out behavior.
- Stable outputs: outputs are the contract. Additive changes only by default; breaking changes require a major-version bump and documented migration recipe.
- Signal-first design: modules should emit a small set of lifecycle signals (outputs + tags + state hints) to help higher-level orchestration detect drift and compatibility.
- Testable upgrades: every module must include an upgrade playbook and a few acceptance tests (smoke for create/destroy, idempotency, and two-step upgrade).

Surface conventions (high level)
- Naming: module inputs and outputs use snake_case. Keep names short but explicit: vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids, iam_role_arn, cluster_endpoint.
- Inputs: group inputs into required/contextual/advanced. Required: things that cannot be determined (account_id, cidr_block for on-prem overlay). Contextual: environment, region, tags. Advanced: features behind booleans (enable_flow_logs, use_secondary_cidr).
- Outputs: only material resources and simple computed values. Prefer IDs and ARNs rather than complex maps. Avoid exposing provider objects or nested maps unless consumer use-case justifies it.

Standard variable blocks (recommendation)
- required variables (explicit):
  - string account_id (no default)
  - string environment (default: "dev" but no magic; prefer explicit on prod)
  - string name_prefix (default: "rdw")
- optional variables with safe defaults:
  - string region (default: provider region)
  - bool enable_flow_logs (default: false)
  - list(string) public_cidr_overrides (default: [])

Example minimal variable doc snippet (for module README):
"""
variable "account_id" {
  description = "AWS account id where resources are created"
  type        = string
}
variable "enable_flow_logs" {
  description = "Enable VPC flow logs to the configured log destination"
  type        = bool
  default     = false
}
"""

Outputs contract (must-haves)
- vpc_id: string (primary contract)
- public_subnet_ids: list(string)
- private_subnet_ids: list(string)
- nat_gateway_ids: list(string) (when applicable)
- route_table_ids: list(string)
- resource_tags: map(string) (lightweight map of tags used on top-level resources)
- stability_signal: string (see below)

Stability signal and state hints
Every module must return a stability_signal output which encodes: module_semver | last_change_ts | compatibility_score. The format is intentionally terse to be machine-parsable, e.g. "v1.2.0|2024-02-10T14:00Z|ok". The CI tooling will read stability_signal and surface warnings for anything with a score != ok.
Notes on scoring (adopt simple set): ok, warn, breaking. Scoring is computed by module reviewers and set as metadata in the module.

Versioning and upgrade policy
- Follow semver-like numbering but we only bump major for breaking API changes. Patch/minor can include new optional inputs and additive outputs.
- Deprecation period: when removing an output or changing an output shape, do a deprecation release that:
  1) Adds a new output (name v2 or new suffix) and emits a deprecation_message output pointing consumers to migration notes.
  2) Wait at least two release cycles across downstream stacks (tracked by tags) before removing.
- Upgrade tests: each module must include an explicit two-stage upgrade test in CI: 
  - Provision baseline with vN (smoke)
  - Apply upgrade to vN+1 and validate no diff on existing resources except what is intended.

Backward/forward compatibility checklist for reviewers
- Are all existing outputs still present and typed as before?
- Are any new required inputs introduced? If so, can they be auto-computed or should the module bump major?
- Has behaviour behind booleans been flipped? Document and add a temporary compatibility flag.
- Do variable defaults create new external side effects? (e.g., enabling flow logs by default)

EKS/GKE/AKS cluster primitive specifics
- Expose cluster endpoint, certificate data, kubeconfig (as a generated file path or as a token string — prefer token output + an action to materialize file off-band), node_group_ids, node_role_arn, control_plane_security_group_id.
- Don’t bake cluster-level addons as defaults. Provide capability flags (enable_istio = false) and separate module or submodule for addons.
- Upgrade path for control plane version bumps: expose desired_k8s_version and current_k8s_version (computed). Provide an output cluster_upgrade_plan_url which points to a minimal runbook (can be generated in CI as a gist or Confluence link).

IAM primitives guidance
- Provide role ARNs and policy ARNs only; avoid returning large policy documents in outputs.
- Inputs should accept principal tags and an optional external_id for cross-account roles.
- For SAM/IRSA (service account roles), provide a mapping output: service_account_name -> role_arn. Keep the mapping flat (no nested objects).

Testing and acceptance (must have)
- Unit: terraform validate + linters (tflint, checkov) on every PR.
- Integration: smoke create/destroy in an isolated account. Keep test resources small and timeout-friendly.
- Upgrade: the two-stage upgrade test described above.
- Contract tests: a simple harness that validates presence and typing of required outputs and rejects when shape changes unexpectedly.

Outputs/variables example (practical)
Outputs block (recommended minimal):
"""
output "vpc_id" {
  description = "ID of the created VPC"
  value       = aws_vpc.main.id
}

output "public_subnet_ids" {
  description = "List of public subnet IDs"
  value       = aws_subnet.public.*.id
}

output "stability_signal" {
  description = "Module stability signal: semver|ts|score"
  value       = join("|", [local.module_version, timestamp(), local.stability_score])
}
"""

Migration playbook template (short)
1) Create a branch and bump module to vN+1 (if non-breaking, follow minor/patch rules).
2) Run the contract test harness against representative stacks in staging.
3) If harness passes: create a canary upgrade PR for a single low-risk stack (tagged canary).
4) Monitor stability_signal of dependent stacks; if score != ok, pause and open an incident for manual review.
5) Roll out to additional stacks in waves (20%, 50%, 100%).
6) After 30 days with no regressions, consider deprecations/cleanup.

Operational signals to emit (implementation suggestions)
- Add lightweight tags on created resources with keys: rdw:module, rdw:version, rdw:stack. Useful for audits and for orchestration to correlate resources with deployments.
- Emit an SSM parameter (or equivalent) per stack with the module_version for quick lookup in air-gapped environments.
- Produce a minimal JSON artifact (artifact_url output) that CI uploads after an apply: {module, version, timestamp, resources_count, outputs_snapshot_url}. Keep artifact size small.

Common pitfalls and anti-patterns
- Exposing provider IDs or raw provider objects as outputs. These are brittle and leak implementation.
- Making boolean defaults that change network topology (don’t flip cidr_defaults).
- Outputs that include secrets: never output raw secrets (use references to vault/params).

Open questions / TODOs
- Standardize a single stability_score computation algorithm (should it be CI-determined or reviewer-set?). Suggested near-term: reviewer-set in module metadata, automated checks for common issues will surface warnings.
- Decide on canonical artifact storage for artifact_url (S3 vs internal blobstore) for private deployments (air-gapped constraints).
- Finalize the deprecation cadence for outputs (currently suggested: two release cycles).

Notes to reviewers
- When approving a module change, explicitly check the stability_signal change. If stability_score is anything other than "ok", require an explicit justification and make sure the migration playbook is linked.

References and links
- Internal: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules (main repo)
- Ticket examples: jira/PD-987 (upgrade tests for vpc module), jira/TF-204 (stability_signal proposal)
